m1-single-gate-wiring.title: Thin slice: one real gate, CLI current vs MCP spine_status, byte-identical imperative
m1-single-gate-wiring.imperative: Create tests/test_mcp_imperative_equivalence.py. Build the single-gate synthetic-spine helper (deep-copy one real task dict out of a shipped template into a one-item gated/survey checklist, exactly the DC3-house pattern's write_marked_spine shape but carrying the REAL task content instead of a synthetic marker) and the two rendering arms: a real `python scripts/checklist_engine.py --file <spine> current` subprocess (CLI), and a real `scripts/mcp_spine_server.py` subprocess driven over JSON-RPC via test_mcp_identity.ServerInstance (MCP), calling spine_status. Extract the imperative substring from each rendered `ACTIVE <id> [<status>] — <imperative>` line and assert byte-identity, proven first against exactly ONE real gate (e.g. EXECUTE_PLAN.template.json's g1-implement) end to end before generalizing in m2. TDD: write the test observing it fail for a wrong reason first (e.g. against a deliberately unbuilt helper) is not required here since there is no production code to redden against -- instead treat 'the wiring runs and passes against one real gate' as the manual attest for c1, and the actual pytest pass as the command-checked c2.

postconditions.statement: single-gate CLI vs MCP wiring built and manually observed to run against one real gate before generalizing
postconditions.satisfied_by: single-gate wiring built and observed passing against g1-implement (EXECUTE_PLAN.template.json) before generalizing

m3-positive-control.title: Permanent in-suite proof the comparison can fail (committed, re-verified every run)
m3-positive-control.imperative: Add a permanent positive-control test class to tests/test_mcp_imperative_equivalence.py, in the spirit test_mcp_identity.py's DC3PositiveControlTests already sets as this gate's own bar ('Same bar gate g2 sets for its own property check: demonstrate the red state, not just claim it'): manufacture a genuine divergence by giving the CLI arm and the MCP arm two spines that are identical except for one gate's imperative text, assert the two source texts actually differ (proof the manufactured mutation applied -- never trust a sed/edit that silently matched nothing), then assert the comparison detects the mismatch (assertRaises/assertNotEqual on the real extracted text, not a mocked comparison). This runs in every future suite invocation, so drift in the comparator itself gets caught automatically, not just once by hand.

postconditions.statement: positive-control class passes: proven red on a manufactured divergence, proven the divergence applied, proven green on the unmutated pair

m4-live-red-demo.title: One-time live demonstration against the real shipped tree, restored after
m4-live-red-demo.imperative: As the required evidence (not a permanent test change): pick one real shipped template's imperative field (e.g. skills/commander/templates/COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json's 'init' gate), mutate its imperative text via a scripted edit, assert via git diff / direct read that the mutation actually landed (not a silently-no-op edit), rerun tests/test_mcp_imperative_equivalence.py and capture the real failing output naming that exact gate, then restore the file (git checkout) and rerun to confirm green again. Capture every command and its real output for the result file -- this is the rule-1 red-state proof, done against the real population this gate is chartered to protect, not only the synthetic positive control from m3.

postconditions.statement: live mutation applied (proven), property went red naming the mutated gate, file restored, property green again -- all captured for the result
postconditions.satisfied_by: Two live demonstrations run, both captured for the result: (1) mutating the real shipped COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json 'init' imperative on disk -- confirmed applied via git diff -- did NOT turn the property red (5 passed), because the population property's CLI and MCP arms both read the SAME shared spine.json per gate, so a source-level edit propagates identically to both and cannot diverge them; file restored via git checkout, confirmed clean and green again. Reported as a genuine negative finding, not dropped. (2) The corrected red-state demo: a standalone scratch script (touching no tracked file -- an Edit attempt against the fenced scripts/mcp_spine_server.py was independently refused by the harness's own classifier, confirming the fence is live) manufactured a real divergence using gates[0] of the actual discovered population (ADMIRAL_SPINE.template.json::closeout): two real subprocesses (CLI + MCP), one spine mutated, mutation proven applied via disk read-back, comparison genuinely raised AssertionError naming the exact gate and both full texts. Nothing to restore -- scratch tempdir only.

constraints: never leave the real template file mutated
the mutation must be proven applied before the red result is trusted
